subject: AP Calculus AB
seed_class: D handled under the class-B clean-room path (same Product Owner decision as the AP Chemistry batch, DECISION-0098)
extractor_note: Written by the extractor context, the only context that read the source. Patterns only: no source functions, intervals, numbers, wording, choices or answer values. Units 1-3 only, so the source's Unit 5 item is excluded. 3 members per family: v1 easy, v2 medium, v3 hard; each member uses a different function and interval from its siblings.

families.task_verb: Compute the average rate of change of a trigonometric function on an interval, using exact values
families.structure: A sine or cosine function with a coefficient inside the argument, possibly plus a vertical shift or an outside coefficient, on an interval whose endpoints are multiples of pi. Members must include: one interval on which the endpoint values are equal, so the average rate of change is zero even though the function is not constant there; one whose exact answer has pi in the denominator; and one in a context with units, for example a periodic quantity over time. No calculator: values must come from the unit circle.
misconceptions: Evaluates the derivative at an endpoint or at the midpoint, giving an instantaneous rate instead of the average
Drops the coefficient inside the argument when evaluating, for example using the value at x instead of at kx
Gives the change in the function without dividing by the interval length
Subtracts in the wrong order, so the sign is reversed

families.task_verb: Compare or locate average rates of change across intervals
families.structure: A function given algebraically (polynomial, rational or radical) or as a short table of values. The task is to decide which of four intervals has the greatest (or least, or negative) average rate of change, or which interval has a given average rate of change. Choices are intervals. Members must include one table-based member, one where a function value at a left endpoint is negative, and one in a context with units. Do not simply ask for one average rate of change on one interval: the bank already has several.
misconceptions: Compares function values at the right endpoints instead of rates
Divides by the right endpoint instead of the interval length
Mishandles a negative function value at the left endpoint when subtracting
Uses the mean of the two endpoint values (an average value of the function) instead of the average rate of change
families.avoid_overlap: Existing bank items ask for one average rate of change of x^2-3x, t^2+4t, sqrt(x) and x^3-x on fixed intervals, plus limit-of-average-velocity and table-of-h items. Do not reuse those functions or that task shape.
